source_name: CeJN - Centralni elektronski sistem javnih nabavki Crne Gore (portal home)
why_relevant: Single legally mandated national e-procurement system for Montenegro (live since 1 Jan 2021, built by Belit for the Ministry of Finance / Directorate for Public Procurement Policy with EU IPA funding). All stages - procurement plans, public calls, tender documentation, decisions, complaints, contracts and execution reports - must pass through it, so banking/payments-adjacent lots (POS terminals, card personalisation, payment gateways, cash handling, self-service kiosks, core banking/treasury software) surface here first and in full technical detail.

source_name: CeJN - Tenderi (live tender notice listing)
why_relevant: The actual live notice feed of the national portal: open calls with deadlines, contracting authority, estimated value and downloadable tender documentation. This is the A2 spine - the first place a Montenegrin POS/payments/self-service/cash-handling lot becomes visible with specifications.

source_name: Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki (Directorate for Public Procurement Policy, Ministry of Finance)
why_relevant: Policy owner and system operator behind CeJN. Publishes the legal framework, sub-regulations (pravilnici), registration instructions for economic operators, reform strategies/action plans and aggregate annual procurement reports. Essential for interpreting notice fields, thresholds, and for knowing which procedures are exempt from CeJN publication.

source_name: eTender Portal UJN CG (legacy pre-2021 notice archive)
why_relevant: The predecessor national notice portal (Delta 2015 platform) still exposes a free, unauthenticated notice search. Gives historical baseline of Montenegrin banking/payments procurement before the CeJN cut-over on 1 Jan 2021 - incumbent suppliers, prior award values, recurring contracting authorities.

source_name: wapi.gov.me - Government of Montenegro document/file API
why_relevant: The shared file-delivery endpoint behind gov.me sites; tender documentation, draft pravilnici, commission decisions and ministry annexes are served from /download/{uuid}?version=1.0 and /download-preview/{uuid}. Useful both as a direct document fetch path and as a fingerprint for locating official PDFs indexed by search engines but not linked on portal front-ends.

source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki - Rješenja (appeals decisions)
why_relevant: Appeal body for public procurement and PPP award procedures. Its published rješenja (decisions) reveal contested banking/payments tenders, the actual bidders and their objections, tailored technical specifications, and annulled/repeated procedures - often the richest competitive-intelligence text in the whole A2 workstream, richer than the notice itself.

source_name: Državna revizorska institucija Crne Gore (State Audit Institution) - audit reports
why_relevant: Audits individual budget users and the procurement system itself, naming contracts, values, irregularities and suppliers. Its reports on bodies such as Uprava prihoda i carina and state agencies expose payments/IT contracts, direct awards and framework agreements that are hard to reconstruct from notices alone.

source_name: nabavke.com - regional procurement aggregator (Montenegro / CeJN mirror)
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator covering RS/ME/BA/MK/HR/SI that republishes Montenegrin CeJN notices AND rehosts the original tender documents under its own /tdoc-cejn/documents/ path. Extremely useful as a scrape-friendly, server-rendered fallback when CeJN's SPA blocks automated collection, and as a way to recover documents withdrawn from the official portal.

source_name: javne-nabavke.com - Montenegro tender section
why_relevant: Second regional aggregator with a Montenegro vertical and branch/sector taxonomy (e.g. electro-installations, IT), giving an alternative categorisation of the same CeJN notice flow plus commentary/how-to content that reveals procedural practice.

source_name: Centralna banka Crne Gore - Tenderi i oglasi
source_subtype: contracting authority own tender page (central bank)
why_relevant: The central bank is itself a contracting authority and the single most payments-relevant buyer in Montenegro (RTGS/instant payments, SEPA alignment, card/coin production, banking IT). It publishes its own tender and notice page in parallel to CeJN, sometimes with fuller technical annexes and with non-ZJN calls (design competitions, sale/lease notices) that never appear on the national portal.

source_name: World Bank Procurement Notices (Finances One) - Montenegro / TIPS Clone & SEPA project
why_relevant: The World Bank approved a EUR 8m loan (July 2025) for the Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization and SEPA Alignment (TIPS Clone) Project - instant payments infrastructure for CBCG. IFI-financed procurement runs under Bank rules and its notices/contract awards appear here (and in STEP), often BEFORE or instead of full publication on CeJN. This is the single most important non-CeJN channel for Montenegrin payments-infrastructure tenders.

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP) - Montenegro notices
why_relevant: EBRD-financed public-sector projects in Montenegro (utilities, municipalities, transport, financial sector TC) procure goods/consultancy through ECEPP rather than CeJN. Captures cash-handling, ticketing/fare-collection, billing and financial-sector advisory lots that the national portal misses.

source_name: EU Publications Office - public procurement / TED procurement details for Montenegro
why_relevant: EU-funded (IPA) contracts implemented in Montenegro are advertised through EU channels; CeJN itself was built under an IPA-funded project. Gives visibility of EU-financed IT/payments and institution-building lots located in Podgorica that are outside the national ZJN regime.

source_name: MANS - Javne nabavke (procurement watchdog category & institution profiles)
why_relevant: MANS is Montenegro's most active anti-corruption NGO monitoring procurement (participant in the regional Balkan Tender Watch project). It profiles institutions such as the Commission for Protection of Rights, publishes FOI-obtained contracts and investigative analyses - a route to contract texts and award details not visible on CeJN.

source_name: Paragraf.me - Zakon o javnim nabavkama Crne Gore (consolidated law)
why_relevant: Consolidated text of the Montenegrin Public Procurement Act with amendments. Defines which entities are obliged contracting authorities (explicitly including the Central Bank), thresholds, procedure types, the 'jednostavne nabavke' simple-procurement regime and mandatory publication duties - i.e. the rules that determine what is and is not visible on CeJN.

source_name: Pravilnik o načinu sprovođenja jednostavnih nabavki (simple-procurement rulebook, UJN)
why_relevant: Defines the below-threshold regime (goods/services up to EUR 15,000, works up to EUR 30,000) handled outside full CeJN procedures and reported only in semi-annual reports (1 Jan-30 Jun, 1 Jul-31 Dec). Directly explains a structural blind spot for small POS/terminal/maintenance orders and points to where those purchases can still be recovered.

source_name: Municipal procurement pages (e.g. Opština Bar - Javne nabavke; Komunalne usluge Podgorica)
source_subtype: contracting authority own procurement page (local government / utility)
why_relevant: Municipalities and municipal utilities are heavy buyers of billing systems, cash-collection, self-service kiosks and card acceptance for utility payments. They mirror their CeJN notices locally and additionally publish procurement plans and simple-procurement lists that never reach the national portal, plus signed contracts.

source_name: Uprava prihoda i carina (Revenue & Customs Administration) - fiscalisation & procurement
why_relevant: Owner of Montenegro's electronic fiscalisation system (efi/eFaktura), the state actor whose rules and procurements shape the POS/fiscal-device and certificate market. Publishes draft pravilnici, technical specifications for fiscalisation software, and is a recurring contracting authority for payments-adjacent IT; also audited by DRI with contract detail.

source_name: Pošta Crne Gore - e-servisi / elektronska fiskalizacija and procurement
why_relevant: State-owned Post is simultaneously a contracting authority, a payments/cash-handling operator and a distribution channel for fiscalisation certificates. Its service pages reveal the operating ecosystem (certificate issuers: Pošta, Crnogorski Telekom, CoreIT) and therefore the local vendor landscape that bids on CeJN payments lots.

source_name: Belit d.o.o. - vendor of the CeJN platform (product page)
why_relevant: The company that built CeJN for the Montenegrin Ministry of Finance under an EC/IPA-funded project. Vendor documentation describes the system's modules and data model (planning, notices, decisions, complaints, contracts, execution reports), which is the fastest way to understand what data fields and endpoints a collector can expect from CeJN.

source_name: CeJN Crna Gora - official Facebook page
why_relevant: Operational announcement channel for the portal: outages, migrations, new modules, deadline changes and training. Cheap early-warning signal that a collector's assumptions about CeJN structure are about to break.

source_name: Montenegro-focused commercial tender aggregators (montenegrotenders.com, tendersontime, globaltenders, tendersinfo)
why_relevant: English-language commercial mirrors of Montenegrin tender flow. Low intrinsic credibility and heavy paywalling, but useful for English keyword discovery, for spotting notices whose Montenegrin wording our glossary misses, and as an availability cross-check when CeJN is unreachable.

source_name: Nabavke.com — Portal javnih nabavki (private mirror/aggregator of CEJN documents)
source_subtype: commercial tender/contract aggregator with document mirror
why_relevant: Mirrors CEJN procurement records as stable, directly-fetchable HTML pages and PDFs, including award decisions. A confirmed document pattern is https://www.nabavke.com/tdoc-cejn/documents/{id}-{timestamp}-Odluka_o_izboru_najpovoljnije_ponude_{id}.pdf and a per-procurement page pattern /javne-nabavke-tenderi-crna-gora/{predmet-slug}/{narucilac-slug}/{grad}/{id}. The 'tdoc-cejn' path indicates it re-serves CEJN tender documentation, which makes it far easier to harvest than CEJN itself.
